title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
description: Build a set of distinct values, find the start of each consecutive run, and track the longest run.
note: A value starts a run only when its predecessor is absent. Skipping other values prevents repeatedly scanning the same sequence.
notes: set(nums) constructs a fresh set[int] without modifying the input. Duplicates appear once. Birdie visits distinct values in first-appearance order, making traversal reproducible; the returned length is independent of that order.
The predecessor check uses continue to skip values inside an existing run. Starting at its smallest value, the while loop counts the run by checking successive integers.

max!(longestSeq, currSeq) updates the initialized accumulator only when the candidate is larger. It is a built-in statement whose first argument is a writable location; max(longestSeq, currSeq) remains a value-returning function call.

Each distinct value is part of exactly one scanned run, so the nested loop does not repeatedly scan every suffix. Under constant-cost hashing and integer-operation assumptions, the algorithm takes expected O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.

An empty input returns zero. Negative values and duplicate values need no separate cases. Birdie’s arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic avoids fixed-width overflow when checking predecessor and successor values.
